stem: The consumer price index for 2025 with base year 2015 = 100 stands at 125. What is the purchasing power of a rupee in 2025 relative to 2015, expressed as a fraction of a rupee?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Purchasing power = 100 / price index = 100 / 125 = 0.80. One rupee in 2025 buys only 80 paise worth of goods compared with 2015 prices.
Dividing the index by 100 (125/100 = 1.25) gives the inverse: the number of current rupees needed to equal one base-year rupee, not the purchasing power.
Taking only the rise in the index (125 - 100 = 25) and expressing it as 0.25 treats the 25-point increase as the purchasing power rather than using the full 125 in the formula.
Reporting the index value of 125 as the purchasing power confuses the index number itself with the reciprocal measure of purchasing power.

explanation: Purchasing power of money = 100 / price index = 100 / 125 = 0.80. This means Rs 1 in 2025 has the same buying power as Rs 0.80 had in 2015 - prices have risen 25%, so the rupee has weakened accordingly.

explanation_sections.punchline: Purchasing power is the reciprocal of the price index ratio: 100 / index, not the index itself.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula: Purchasing power = 100 / price index. Map: index = 125. Compute: 100 / 125 = 0.80.
explanation_sections.lesson: Higher price index always means lower purchasing power. The two move in opposite directions - a fundamental check.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 seconds. Trap: option 2 (Rs 1.25) is what you get when you invert the formula. If the index is above 100, purchasing power must be below 1.
